newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to extend $1.5 billion in loans to China.
newsitem.headline: Japan to extend $1.5 billion in loans to China.

text.p: Japan announced on Tuesday it had agreed to extend 170 billion yen ($1.5 billion) in low-interest untied loans to China.
But it stopped short of resuming grant aid that has been frozen for 17 months because of Beijing's nuclear testing.
The loans announced on Tuesday were the first tranche in a loan package Japan had pledged to China for the next three years.
The loans, to be extended in the fiscal year ending next March, will cover 22 projects, the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
Officials from Japan and China exchanged documents on the loans in Beijing, the ministry said.
Japan had pledged to extend about 580 billion yen ($5 billion) in yen loans between 1996-1999, but talks on the provision of the loans had been delayed for several months.
Japan had sent no missions to approve projects for the package since China conducted a nuclear test in May.
A mission was finally sent to Beijing late last month.
Japanese officials did not formally say whether China's nuclear testing affected the timing of the loan provision.
Japan froze grant aid, worth about seven billion yen ($61.4 million), in August 1995 as a mainly symbolic protest at China's nuclear test programme. ($1=114 yen)
